Confirmed OPEN DECISION resolution (c) -- unconditional notification -- is correct given the real code path. Remedy 2 is confirmed to be a correctness backstop independent of Remedy 1's delivery mechanism succeeding.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system/extensions/core's /orchestrate Move 2 (skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md) forwards only `agent` (subagent_type) and `model` as Agent-tool arguments when dispatching -- no dispatched agent receives a `name:` parameter, and SendMessage is not used anywhere in the core extension for cross-dispatch coordination (one unrelated hit in hooks/please-grant.sh). Any future design assuming one live dispatch can SendMessage another live sibling dispatch by name needs a prerequisite Move 2 naming-convention change (or a different mechanism, e.g. a file sentinel) -- it is not already supported.

The aux-dispatch consume-and-clear pattern (.blocker-research.json/.drift-inspection.json, consumed by orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's AUX DECISION block on a LATER cycle) is the only existing cross-dispatch file-signaling precedent in agent-system/extensions/core. It is orchestrator-mediated and cross-cycle, not agent-mediated and intra-cycle -- a genuinely new consumption model (a live implement dispatch polling a sentinel file written by a concurrently-running aux dispatch, within the same cycle) would be the first of its kind if built.

agent-system/extensions/core's ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE (scripts/verify-deploy.sh) now defaults to 'hard', not 'warn' -- task #289 already landed this promotion. skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's ceiling was raised to 21,500 B alongside that work, but current measurement (wc -c) is 21,476 B: only 24 B of headroom. Any task touching SKILL.md must verify the live byte count at plan/implement time rather than trusting an older task description's snapshot, since this ceiling/measurement pair changes frequently (see context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json's own derivation history).
